title: COSI — Message Envelope
description: Top-level wrapper for all COSI messages. Common fields are validated here; the payload is validated against the schema that matches assetClass.

messageID.description: Globally unique UUID v5 for this message instance. Producers allocate distinct generation inputs for distinct instances, even with identical content. Retries and replays preserve the assigned ID, including across restart; UUID v5 alone does not ensure uniqueness or de-duplication.

correlationID.description: UUID v5 linking related messages. Required on setup-response: the messageID of the original setup request.

assetClass.description: Identifies the business domain of this message. Determines which payload schema applies.

messageType.description: hbt = Heartbeat (periodic, min every 5 s). cos = Change-of-Status (event-driven). onetime = Static reference data sent once.

machineId.description: Plant-owned machine identifier, unique within its site and matching the machine topic segment. Providers map their identifiers to the plant definition.

oneOf.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the event being reported (not the time the message was created or transmitted). The Z suffix is mandatory; local-time offsets are not allowed (e.g., 2026-04-01T08:23:11.000Z).

timestamp.description: Original event time in UTC Z form; required null only for the dedicated Last Will, whose future publication time is unknown at registration.

status.description: Machine state at the event time. offline is the final controlled-shutdown notification; lastwill is reserved for the dedicated connection-loss notification and does not assert a physical stop.

payload.description: Asset-class-specific data. Schema is determined by assetClass (enforced by the oneOf below).

schemaId.description: Full payload schema identifier, including version; must match assetClass.

connectionId.description: Required on the Will and normal equipment messages of a connection using Last Will. Fresh globally unique UUID v5 per MQTT connection, including reconnect/restart; shared for that connection. Distinct from MQTT client ID and messageID. Allocation method is implementation-defined.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the event being reported (not the time the message was created or transmitted). The Z suffix is mandatory; local-time offsets are not allowed (e.g., 2026-04-01T08:23:11.000Z).
